```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(scales)
library(here)
library(terra)
library(sf)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# Load processed data
db_strict      <- readRDS(here("data/occurrences/processed/db_modelling_strict.rds"))
db_unc         <- readRDS(here("data/occurrences/processed/db_modelling_uncertainty.rds"))
db_thinned     <- readRDS(here("data/occurrences/processed/db_thinned_025.rds"))
species_summary <- readRDS(here("data/occurrences/processed/species_records_summary.rds"))
eoo_all        <- readRDS(here("data/occurrences/processed/eoo_results_025.rds"))
spp_flags      <- readRDS(here("data/occurrences/processed/spp_endemic_flags.rds"))
spp_mod        <- readRDS(here("data/occurrences/processed/spp_endemics_modellable.rds"))
spp_unmod      <- readRDS(here("data/occurrences/processed/spp_endemics_unmodellable.rds"))

# Load evaluation summaries
unc_summary    <- read_csv(here("outputs/evaluation/01_01_uncertainty_filter_summary.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE)
record_class   <- read_csv(here("outputs/evaluation/01_02_record_class_summary.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE)
criteria_summ  <- read_csv(here("outputs/evaluation/01_03_endemism_criteria_summary.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE)
cr_family      <- read_csv(here("outputs/evaluation/01_03_CR_species_by_family.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE)
cr_species     <- read_csv(here("outputs/evaluation/01_03_CR_species_list.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE)
```

# Overview

This document summarises the complete occurrence data preparation pipeline
for the analysis of endemism hotspots of Neotropical vascular epiphytes
under climate and land-use change scenarios. All steps are fully reproducible
via the scripts in `scripts/01_*.R`.

```{r pipeline-summary}
tibble(
  Step = c(
    "Raw database (EpIG-DB 2.0 + GBIF)",
    "01_00 — Uncertainty filter (archived, not applied — see sensitivity & decisions log)",
    "01_01 — Spatial thinning (0.25°)",
    "01_02 — EOO + endemism classification"
  ),
  Records = c(
    format(nrow(db_strict),  big.mark = ","),
    format(nrow(db_unc),     big.mark = ","),
    format(nrow(db_thinned), big.mark = ","),
    "—"
  ),
  Species = c(
    format(n_distinct(db_strict$scientificName),  big.mark = ","),
    format(n_distinct(db_unc$scientificName),     big.mark = ","),
    format(n_distinct(db_thinned$scientificName), big.mark = ","),
    format(nrow(spp_flags), big.mark = ",")
  ),
  Notes = c(
    "Post-cleaning: families + species excluded",
    "Keep NA uncertainty OR <= 27,500 m",
    "1 record per species per 0.25° cell; seed = 123",
    "EOO calculated with ConR (convex hull, exclude.area = FALSE)"
  )
) %>%
  kable(caption = "Data preparation pipeline summary") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

---

# Step 01_00 — Coordinate Uncertainty Filter (archived, not applied)

Records were retained where `coordinateUncertaintyInMeters` was `NA`
(unknown precision, majority of historical herbarium specimens) or
≤ 27,750 m (≈ one cell side at 0.25°: 0.25 × 111,320 m/° = 27,830 m).
Records with uncertainty > 27,750 m were removed because the true location
could fall in a different grid cell at the modelling resolution.

**Decision rationale:** Excluding NA uncertainty records would introduce
a temporal bias toward post-2000 collections and reduce taxonomic coverage
of historically collected taxa. At 0.25° resolution, the cost of retaining
imprecise records is lower than at finer scales.

```{r uncertainty-summary}
unc_summary %>%
  arrange(desc(n_removed)) %>%
  head(15) %>%
  kable(
    caption = "Top 15 families by records removed (coordinate uncertainty filter)",
    digits  = 1
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r uncertainty-totals}
tibble(
  Metric = c("Records before filter", "Records removed",
             "Pct removed", "Records retained", "Species retained"),
  Value  = c(
    format(nrow(db_strict),                        big.mark = ","),
    format(nrow(db_strict) - nrow(db_unc),         big.mark = ","),
    paste0(round((nrow(db_strict) - nrow(db_unc)) /
                   nrow(db_strict) * 100, 1), "%"),
    format(nrow(db_unc),                           big.mark = ","),
    format(n_distinct(db_unc$scientificName),      big.mark = ",")
  )
) %>%
  kable(caption = "Uncertainty filter: overall summary") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

## Sensitivity: effect of the filter on the endemic species pool

The uncertainty filter removes 2.2% of records overall, but the concern is whether
this disproportionately affects rare endemic species with few records. Records
with NA uncertainty are retained (historical specimens); only records with
*reported* uncertainty > `COORD_UNCERT_MAX` (27,750 m) are removed.

This analysis compares, for each species with EOO < 100,000 km², the number of
pre-thinning records with vs. without the filter. Species that would cross the
n = 10 threshold (i.e., modellable without filter, unmodellable with it) are
flagged explicitly.

Note: counts are pre-thinning. Post-thinning n will be lower for both scenarios,
but the *difference* caused by the filter is the relevant quantity here.

References: Moudrý & Šímová (2012) showed that strict uncertainty filters
disproportionately reduce records for rare species. Breiner et al. (2015) —
the ESM paper — does not apply an uncertainty filter. At coarse resolution
(≥ 0.25°), retaining imprecise records is generally preferred for rare taxa.

```{r unc-sensitivity-prep}
THRESH      <- 27750   # COORD_UNCERT_MAX from 00_config.R
MIN_OCC_MOD <- 10      # MIN_OCC from 00_config.R

# Records per species before and after filter (pre-thinning)
n_before_filter <- db_strict %>%
  count(scientificName, name = "n_before")

n_after_filter <- db_unc %>%
  count(scientificName, name = "n_after")

n_removed_by_filter <- db_strict %>%
  filter(!is.na(coordinateUncertaintyInMeters),
         coordinateUncertaintyInMeters > THRESH) %>%
  count(scientificName, name = "n_removed_by_unc_filter")

# Join with EOO flags — focus on endemic pool (EOO < 100,000 km²)
unc_sensitivity <- spp_flags %>%
  filter(endemic_100k) %>%
  dplyr::select(scientificName, family, EOO_km2, endemic_B1) %>%
  left_join(n_before_filter,     by = "scientificName") %>%
  left_join(n_after_filter,      by = "scientificName") %>%
  left_join(n_removed_by_filter, by = "scientificName") %>%
  mutate(
    n_before          = replace_na(n_before, 0L),
    n_after           = replace_na(n_after,  0L),
    n_removed         = replace_na(n_removed_by_unc_filter, 0L),
    mod_with_filter    = n_after  >= MIN_OCC_MOD,
    mod_without_filter = n_before >= MIN_OCC_MOD,
    lost_modellability = mod_without_filter & !mod_with_filter
  )
```

```{r unc-sensitivity-summary}
sens_summary <- tibble(
  Metric = c(
    "Endemic species (EOO < 100k km²)",
    "  — with >= 1 record removed by filter",
    "  — that lose modellability (n_before >= 10, n_after < 10)",
    "  — modellable with filter (n_after >= 10)",
    "  — modellable without filter (n_before >= 10)",
    "Mean n per endemic species — with filter",
    "Mean n per endemic species — without filter",
    "Median n per endemic species — with filter",
    "Median n per endemic species — without filter"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(unc_sensitivity),
    sum(unc_sensitivity$n_removed > 0),
    sum(unc_sensitivity$lost_modellability),
    sum(unc_sensitivity$mod_with_filter),
    sum(unc_sensitivity$mod_without_filter),
    round(mean(unc_sensitivity$n_after,  na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    round(mean(unc_sensitivity$n_before, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    round(median(unc_sensitivity$n_after,  na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    round(median(unc_sensitivity$n_before, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  )
)

sens_summary %>%
  kable(caption = "Sensitivity: uncertainty filter vs. no filter on endemic species pool") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r unc-sensitivity-losers}
# Species that lose modellability because of the filter
lost <- unc_sensitivity %>%
  filter(lost_modellability) %>%
  dplyr::select(scientificName, family, EOO_km2,
                n_without_filter = n_before,
                n_with_filter    = n_after,
                n_removed) %>%
  arrange(n_with_filter)

if (nrow(lost) == 0) {
  cat("No endemic species lose modellability due to the uncertainty filter.\n")
} else {
  lost %>%
    kable(
      caption = paste0(
        "Endemic species that lose modellability (n drops below ",
        MIN_OCC_MOD, ") because of the uncertainty filter"
      ),
      digits = 0
    ) %>%
    kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
}
```

```{r unc-sensitivity-distribution, fig.cap="Distribution of records removed by the uncertainty filter per endemic species (EOO < 100k km²). Most species lose 0 records; species losing 1+ records shown in detail."}
unc_sensitivity %>%
  filter(n_removed > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n_removed)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "#2c7bb6", color = "white") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks()) +
  labs(
    x = "Records removed by uncertainty filter",
    y = "Number of endemic species",
    title = "Records lost per endemic species due to uncertainty filter",
    subtitle = paste0("Only showing species with >= 1 record removed (EOO < 100,000 km²)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Step 01_01 — Spatial Thinning

Occurrences were thinned to one record per species per 0.25° grid cell
(set.seed = 123). This removes spatial redundancy introduced by repeated
sampling at the same or nearby locations, and ensures that each grid cell
contributes at most one data point per species during model calibration.

```{r thinning-summary}
tibble(
  Metric = c("Records before thinning", "Records removed",
             "Pct removed", "Records retained", "Species retained"),
  Value  = c(
    format(nrow(db_unc),                           big.mark = ","),
    format(nrow(db_unc) - nrow(db_thinned),        big.mark = ","),
    paste0(round((nrow(db_unc) - nrow(db_thinned)) /
                   nrow(db_unc) * 100, 1), "%"),
    format(nrow(db_thinned),                       big.mark = ","),
    format(n_distinct(db_thinned$scientificName),  big.mark = ",")
  )
) %>%
  kable(caption = "Spatial thinning: overall summary") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

The high removal rate (58.6%) reflects the well-known sampling bias of
epiphyte occurrence data toward accessible localities (roadsides, biological
stations, botanical gardens), consistent with Svahnström et al. (2025).

## Record classes post-thinning

Species were classified by their number of thinned records to determine
the appropriate modelling approach:

```{r record-classes}
record_class %>%
  kable(
    caption = paste0("Species by record class after thinning to 0.25°.",
                     " MIN_OCC = 5, ESM_THRESHOLD = 25"),
    digits  = 1
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r record-class-bar, fig.height=4}
species_summary %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n_records)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white",
                 alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(5, 25), linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 500),
    labels = c(1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 500)
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = 3,  y = Inf, label = "exclude\n(<5)",
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5, colour = "firebrick") +
  annotate("text", x = 12, y = Inf, label = "ESM\n(5-24)",
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5, colour = "firebrick") +
  annotate("text", x = 80, y = Inf, label = "SDM\n(≥25)",
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5, colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(
    title    = "Distribution of thinned records per species",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines: modelling class thresholds (5 and 25 records)",
    x        = "Thinned records per species (log scale)",
    y        = "Number of species"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

Nearly half of all species (47.3%) have fewer than 5 thinned records and
cannot be modelled with standard SDM approaches. This is consistent with
the high prevalence of rarity in vascular epiphytes documented by
Svahnström et al. (2025), who found that ~45% of epiphyte species have
EOO < 20,000 km².

# Step 01_02 — EOO Calculation and Endemism Classification

## EOO calculation

Extent of Occurrence (EOO) was calculated using the minimum convex hull
method (ConR v2.1; `EOO.computing()`), following IUCN Red List guidelines
v4.0. `exclude.area = FALSE` was used per IUCN recommendation:

> *"The EOO should not be adjusted to exclude obviously unsuitable areas"*
> (IUCN 2022, Guidelines for Using the IUCN Red List Categories and Criteria)

EOO was calculated at 0.25° resolution (consistent with modelling resolution)
on `db_thinned_025`. Species with fewer than 3 unique coordinate pairs
received EOO = NA.

```{r eoo-distribution, fig.height=5}
eoo_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(EOO_km2), EOO_km2 > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = EOO_km2)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white",
                 alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(100, 5000, 20000, 50000, 100000),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick",
             linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_x_log10(
    labels = label_comma(),
    breaks = c(1, 100, 1000, 5000, 20000, 50000, 100000, 1e6, 1e7)
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = 100,    y = Inf, label = "CR",
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3, colour = "firebrick") +
  annotate("text", x = 5000,   y = Inf, label = "EN",
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3, colour = "firebrick") +
  annotate("text", x = 20000,  y = Inf, label = "VU",
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3, colour = "firebrick") +
  annotate("text", x = 50000,  y = Inf, label = "B1",
           vjust = 1.5, size = 3, colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(
    title    = "EOO distribution across Neotropical vascular epiphytes",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines: IUCN thresholds. Species with EOO = NA (< 3 records) excluded.",
    x        = "EOO (km², log scale)",
    y        = "Number of species"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

## Endemism criteria comparison

Five EOO-based endemism criteria were evaluated to select the most
appropriate threshold for defining endemic species:

```{r criteria-table}
criteria_summ %>%
  kable(
    caption = "Species count under alternative endemism criteria",
    digits  = 1
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(4, bold = TRUE, background = "#e8f4f8")  # highlight B1
```

**Selected criterion: EOO < 50,000 km² (IUCN B1)**

This threshold was selected because:
- It corresponds to the IUCN Vulnerable category threshold under criterion B1,
  providing a biologically and conservation-relevant definition of restricted range
- It yields 3,575 endemic species (24% of all species), consistent with
  previous estimates for Neotropical epiphytes
- It provides a defensible, widely-cited threshold comparable across studies

**Sensitivity analysis: EOO < 100,000 km² (broad)**
An alternative threshold will be evaluated in `06_05_hs_sensitivity.R` to
assess whether hotspot patterns are robust to the choice of endemism criterion.

## Modellable vs unmodellable endemics

```{r modellable-summary}
tibble(
  Category = c(
    "Endemic B1 — modellable (n >= 5)",
    "Endemic B1 — unmodellable (n < 5)",
    "Total endemic B1"
  ),
  `N species` = c(
    nrow(spp_mod),
    nrow(spp_unmod),
    nrow(spp_mod) + nrow(spp_unmod)
  ),
  `% of endemic B1` = round(
    c(nrow(spp_mod), nrow(spp_unmod),
      nrow(spp_mod) + nrow(spp_unmod)) /
      (nrow(spp_mod) + nrow(spp_unmod)) * 100, 1
  ),
  Role = c(
    "Main analysis (SDM/ESM projections)",
    "Sensitivity analysis (observed WE only)",
    "—"
  )
) %>%
  kable(caption = "Modellable vs unmodellable endemic species (B1 criterion)") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

Modellable endemics will be further classified as ESM (5–24 records) or
standard SDM (≥ 25 records) in script `01_04_occ_classify_model.R`.

    paste0("Bromeliaceae (", cr_family$n[2], " spp, ",

           round(cr_family$n[3]/120*100), "%)")

```

```{r cr-family-bar, fig.height=4}
cr_family %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(family, n), y = n, fill = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.5) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(direction = -1, option = "magma") +
  ylim(0, max(cr_family$n) * 1.15) +
  labs(
    title    = "Critically Restricted species by family (EOO < 100 km²)",
    subtitle = "All 120 CR species have < 5 thinned records — none modellable",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Number of species"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

All 120 species with EOO < 100 km² have fewer than 5 thinned occurrence
records and cannot be modelled. These ultra-rare species — concentrated in
Orchidaceae (54%), Bromeliaceae (18%), and Araceae (16%) — will contribute
to the sensitivity analysis via their observed occurrence cells only.
This finding highlights a fundamental limitation of occurrence-based
modelling for the most range-restricted Neotropical epiphytes.

# Key Findings and Analytical Implications

## ESM as the dominant modelling approach

```{r esm-sdm-summary}
read_csv(here("outputs/evaluation/01_03_model_class_summary.csv"),
         show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  kable(caption = "Modellable endemic species by modelling approach") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

Of the 1,861 modellable endemic species, **99.4% (n = 1,850) required the
Ensemble of Small Models (ESM) framework** (Lomba et al. 2010; Breiner et al.
2015) due to having fewer than 25 thinned occurrence records. Only 11 species
(0.6%) met the threshold for standard ensemble SDM.

The 11 SDM species share a consistent profile: EOO between 20,000–45,000 km²,
25–37 thinned records, and a concentration in well-sampled Central American
localities (particularly Costa Rica). Araceae dominates this group (4 species:
*Anthurium carnosum*, *A. ranchoanum*, *Philodendron thalassicum*,
*P. brenesii*), followed by Dryopteridaceae (2 *Elaphoglossum* species).

This near-complete dominance of ESM confirms that range restriction and
data scarcity are inseparable in Neotropical vascular epiphytes, and
validates the choice of ESM as the primary modelling framework for this
analysis.

## The unmodellable gap: Critically Restricted species

All 120 species with EOO < 100 km² (Critically Restricted, CR) have
fewer than 5 thinned occurrence records and **cannot be modelled with
any occurrence-based SDM approach**. These species — concentrated in
Orchidaceae (65 spp, 54%), Bromeliaceae (21 spp, 18%), and Araceae
(19 spp, 16%) — represent the most range-restricted epiphytes in the
Neotropics and are precisely the species of greatest conservation concern.

This finding highlights a fundamental limitation of occurrence-based
modelling for conservation: the species most in need of distribution
models are the least amenable to being modelled. Their contribution to
endemism hotspots will be captured through observed occurrence cells
in the sensitivity analysis (`06_05_hs_sensitivity.R`).

## Implications for hotspot analysis

Given that 1,714 endemic B1 species are unmodellable (n < 5 records),
the main analysis (modelled WE) captures only **52% of endemic B1
species**. The sensitivity analysis comparing modelled vs observed
weighted endemism will be essential to assess whether hotspot patterns
are robust to this modelling gap.

```{r implications-table}
tibble(
  Component = c(
    "Main analysis (modelled WE)",
    "Sensitivity analysis (observed WE)",
    "Total endemic B1"
  ),
  Species = c(
    nrow(spp_mod),
    nrow(spp_unmod),
    nrow(spp_mod) + nrow(spp_unmod)
  ),
  `% of B1` = round(
    c(nrow(spp_mod), nrow(spp_unmod),
      nrow(spp_mod) + nrow(spp_unmod)) /
      (nrow(spp_mod) + nrow(spp_unmod)) * 100, 1
  ),
  Method = c(
    "SDM/ESM projections → predicted distribution maps",
    "Observed thinned records → occurrence cells only",
    "—"
  )
) %>%
  kable(caption = "Coverage of endemic B1 species in main vs sensitivity analysis") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

# Environmental Layers

## Climate variables — CHELSA v2.1

Six bioclimatic variables were selected based on empirical support for
vascular epiphytes (see Table S4 in supplementary): bio1 (mean annual
temperature), bio4 (temperature seasonality), bio12 (annual
precipitation), bio14 (precipitation of driest month), bio15
(precipitation seasonality), and bio19 (precipitation of coldest
quarter). All variables were obtained from CHELSA v2.1
(Karger et al. 2017; 1981–2010 baseline) and resampled to 0.25°
resolution using bilinear interpolation, then cropped and masked to
the Neotropical region (Morrone 2022).

For future projections, only bio1, bio4, bio12, and bio15 are available
in CHELSA CMIP6. Variables bio14 and bio19 are not available for future
scenarios and are therefore used only for present-day model calibration.
Final variable selection per species is performed within the calibration
area (area M) using `select07_cv()` (Zurell 2020; Dormann et al. 2013).

```{r correlation-heatmap, fig.cap="Global Spearman correlation matrix for current environmental layers."}
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "data_summary",
                              "02_06_correlation_heatmap.png"))
```

High correlations (|r| > 0.7) identified at the Neotropical scale:
bio14 ~ bio15 (r = −0.86), bio12 ~ bio19 (r = 0.78),
bio12 ~ primf (r = 0.79), bio4 ~ bio12 (r = −0.72).
Variable selection per species within area M will resolve these
collinearities before modelling.

**Note on topography:** Topographic variables were excluded because at
0.25° resolution they are largely collinear with climate variables and
do not provide independent predictive power for epiphyte distributions.

## Land use variables — LUH2 v2

Land use was represented using two continuous variables from the Land
Use Harmonization 2 dataset (LUH2 v2; Hurtt et al. 2020): `primf`
(primary forest fraction per cell) and `secdf` (secondary forest
fraction per cell). These variables were selected over categorical land
use datasets (e.g. Chen et al. 2022) because they provide continuous
measures of forest availability — ecologically more relevant for
epiphytes, which are obligate forest-dwellers, than binary
presence/absence of forest.

LUH2 is provided at 0.25° resolution (native), aligned to the CHELSA
template. For the present, year 2015 was extracted from the historical
states file (LUH2 v2h). For future projections, representative years
were extracted for each 30-year period: **2055** for 2041–2070 and
**2085** for 2071–2100, under SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5.

### Exploration of land use change patterns

```{r luh2-current, fig.cap="Primary (primf) and secondary (secdf) forest fraction in 2015."}
primf <- terra::rast(here("layers", "current", "primf.tif"))
secdf <- terra::rast(here("layers", "current", "secdf.tif"))

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(primf, main = "Primary forest fraction 2015",
     col = viridis::viridis(100))
plot(secdf, main = "Secondary forest fraction 2015",
     col = viridis::viridis(100))
```

Primary forest is concentrated in the Amazon basin and remote Andean
slopes. Secondary forest is highest in Mesoamerica, the Atlantic
Forest, and Andean foothills — areas with historical disturbance and
regeneration. This pattern is consistent with known epiphyte sampling
bias toward accessible, disturbed areas.

```{r luh2-delta, fig.cap="Change in primary forest fraction (Δprimf) under three SSPs, 2015 to 2085."}
primf_126 <- terra::rast(here("layers","future",
                               "gfdl-esm4_ssp126_2071-2100","primf.tif"))
primf_370 <- terra::rast(here("layers","future",
                               "gfdl-esm4_ssp370_2071-2100","primf.tif"))
primf_585 <- terra::rast(here("layers","future",
                               "gfdl-esm4_ssp585_2071-2100","primf.tif"))

diff_126 <- primf_126 - primf
diff_370 <- primf_370 - primf
diff_585 <- primf_585 - primf

pal <- colorRampPalette(c("red", "white", "darkgreen"))(100)
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
plot(diff_126, main = "Δ primf SSP1-2.6", col = pal, range = c(-0.8, 0))
plot(diff_370, main = "Δ primf SSP3-7.0", col = pal, range = c(-0.8, 0))
plot(diff_585, main = "Δ primf SSP5-8.5", col = pal, range = c(-0.8, 0))
```

All scenarios project net loss of primary forest across the Neotropics.
SSP3-7.0 shows the highest mean loss (−6.1% per cell), while SSP5-8.5
has the most extreme local losses (up to −97.3%). Severe losses are
geographically concentrated in the arc of deforestation
(southern Brazil, Bolivia), rather than in the Andes where endemic
epiphyte hotspots are expected. This has important implications: for
Andean endemics, **climate change may be a stronger driver of range
loss than land use change**, while for lowland species the reverse
may be true.

```{r luh2-stats}
tibble(
  SSP  = c("SSP1-2.6", "SSP3-7.0", "SSP5-8.5"),
  mean_delta_primf = c(-0.041, -0.061, -0.055),
  min_delta_primf  = c(-0.803, -0.911, -0.973)
) %>%
  kable(caption = "Mean and minimum change in primary forest fraction 2015–2085 by SSP (GFDL-ESM4)",
        col.names = c("SSP", "Mean Δprimf", "Min Δprimf")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

# Pilot Species

Six species were selected to test the modelling pipeline before
full-scale implementation. Selection criteria: family diversity,
range of EOO values, range of occurrence record counts, and geographic
coverage of major Neotropical biomes.

    "Psychilis krugii",
    "Anthurium dichrophyllum",
    "Peperomia saintpauliella",

    "Maxillaria embreei"
  ),
  Family = c("Orchidaceae", "Araceae", "Piperaceae",
             "Bromeliaceae", "Orchidaceae", "Orchidaceae"),
  n_records = c(5, 5, 6, 9, 12, 10),
  EOO_km2   = c(209, 416, 2218, 16220, 12430, 49837),
  Region    = c("Caribbean (island)", "Colombia/Panama",
                "Colombia (Andes)", "Brazil (dry forest)",

) %>%
  kable(caption = "Pilot species for modelling pipeline testing") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

# Pending Decisions

The following methodological decisions are documented here for
discussion with the thesis committee:

1. **Dispersal assumption:** Full dispersal vs. no dispersal vs.
   buffer (~50–100 km per 30-year period) for future projections.
   Literature review for epiphyte dispersal biology pending.

2. **Endemism threshold for modelling:** Use broadest definition
   (EOO < 100,000 km²) as modelling pool; WE continuous without
   threshold as main hotspot metric; B1/VU/EN as secondary criteria
   for interpretation and vulnerability assessment.

3. **WE_modelled vs WE_observed:** Main analysis uses predicted
   distributions (1,861 spp); complementary analysis uses observed
   thinned records for all B1 endemics (3,575 spp). Comparison will
   assess whether hotspot geography is robust to the modelling gap.

4. **Area M definition:** Calibration using ecorregions containing
   occurrences + buffer; projection using dispersal buffer per period
   (TBD after literature review).



## Area M: Calibration Area Definition {#sec-areaM}

### Comparación de enfoques (especies piloto, mayo 2026)

Se compararon visualmente dos aproximaciones usando las 6 especies piloto:

**Opción A — M por ecorregiones:**
Ecorregiones de Olson con ≥1 ocurrencia + todas las ecorregiones adyacentes
que toca el buffer familiar. *Problema:* el corredor andino conecta Ecuador con
Patagonia (~40°S) en 4/6 especies — biogeográficamente indefendible.

**Opción B — Buffer 200 km:**
Buffer circular simple. *Problema:* demasiado pequeño para especies con
distribuciones disyuntas o muy restringidas.

**Enfoque híbrido propuesto (pendiente de prueba):**
Ecorregiones con ocurrencias + adyacentes de primer orden únicamente,
intersectado con un cap máximo de 500–800 km. Evita la propagación por
corredores manteniendo la lógica biogeográfica.

### Escenarios de dispersal para proyecciones futuras

| Escenario | Definición | Justificación |
|---|---|---|
| Sin dispersal | Especie retenida en M actual | Límite pesimista |
| Dispersal limitado | 1 km/año × período (30 o 60 km) | Conservador, defendible para epífitas |
| Dispersal completo | Todo el Neotrópico climáticamente apto | Límite optimista |

Buffer de calibración por familia (SSC): Orchidaceae 10 km, Bromeliaceae 50 km,
Araceae/Piperaceae 25 km.

> **Pendiente:** revisión de literatura para confirmar tasa 1 km/año en epífitas;
> prueba del M híbrido en especies piloto antes de escalar a 852 spp.


## Area M — final decision {#sec-areaM-final}

Three approaches were compared on 6 pilot species:

1. **Ecoregion-only** — rejected: Andean corridor propagates M from Ecuador to Patagonia in 4/6 species.
2. **Buffer 200 km** — rejected: too small for disjunct or restricted distributions.
3. **Buffer-touched provinces (selected)** — Morrone (2022) provinces containing occurrences + provinces touched by family dispersal buffer (SSC Colombia 2022), with dispersal buffer applied over the province union, clipped to the Neotropics.

M is intentionally broad. Sensitivity analysis planned by varying M definition before scaling to 852 species.

```{r fig-areaM, echo=FALSE}
#| fig-cap: "Area M for 6 pilot species. Blue = calibration area, Red = occurrences."
knitr::include_graphics(here(path_figures, "data_summary", "03_01_pilot_M_areas_final.png"))
```


## ESM implementation notes {#sec-ESM-notes}

Following Breiner et al. (2015), ESMs were calibrated using all bivariate combinations of the 6 predictor variables (15 pairs) with 4 algorithms (GLM, GAM, CTA, SRE) for local/pilot runs, and additionally GBM on HPC (75 models per species). FDA was excluded due to missing dependency (mda package). Models were weighted by Somers D (= 2 x AUC - 1); models with Somers D ≤ 0 were excluded from the ensemble (threshold = 0), following Breiner et al. (2015). The AUC threshold of 0.7 used in early pilots was replaced by Somers D threshold = 0 to avoid over-exclusion of bivariate models for species with small n.

Model evaluation: 5-fold cross-validation with NbRunEval = 3, following pooling evaluation protocol of Collart & Guisan (2023). AUC, TSS, SomersD, and Boyce index reported per species.

**All species use ESM** (no separate SDM pipeline). Methodological justification in `docs/05_decisions_log.qmd` > ESM-only vs. ESM + SDM.

**Minimum sample size:** n ≥ 10 following Breiner et al. (2015). Species with n = 5–9 are **excluded** from modelling; they contribute to occurrence-based WE only (WE_3575 sensitivity analysis, MS2).



## Endemic species pool summary {#sec-endemic-pool}

*This section reads from `spp_endemics_modellable.rds` — outputs auto-update once `01_02_occ_endemics_define.R` is re-run with MIN_OCC = 10 and EOO_BROAD = 100,000 km².*

```{r endemic-pool-load}
# spp_mod already loaded in setup chunk
# pool_available = TRUE if spp_endemics_modellable.rds loaded successfully
pool_available <- exists("spp_mod") && is.data.frame(spp_mod)
if (!pool_available) message("spp_mod not available — re-run 01_02_occ_endemics_define.R with MIN_OCC=10")
```

```{r endemic-pool-overview, eval=pool_available}
#| tbl-cap: "Endemic species pool overview"

tibble(
  Pool = c(
    "Extended modellable (EOO < 100,000 km², n ≥ 10)",
    "B1 modellable (EOO < 50,000 km², n ≥ 10)",
    "Excluded from modelling (n < 10, within EOO < 100,000 km²)"
  ),
  `N species` = c(
    sum(spp_mod$endemic_100k & spp_mod$n_records >= 10),
    sum(spp_mod$b1_pool),

  )
) %>%
  kable() %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

```{r endemic-pool-by-family, eval=pool_available}
#| tbl-cap: "Modellable species by family (EOO < 100,000 km², n ≥ 10). Families with ≥5 species shown."
#| fig-cap: "Species richness of endemic pool by family"

fam_summary <- spp_mod %>%
  filter(endemic_100k, n_records >= 10) %>%
  count(family, name = "n_modellable") %>%
  left_join(
    spp_mod %>%
      filter(endemic_100k, n_records >= 10, b1_pool) %>%
      count(family, name = "n_b1"),
    by = "family"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_modellable))

# M buffer assignment
m_families <- c("Orchidaceae", "Bromeliaceae", "Araceae", "Piperaceae",
                "Dryopteridaceae", "Polypodiaceae", "Gesneriaceae",
                "Melastomataceae", "Clusiaceae", "Begoniaceae",
                "Ericaceae", "Campanulaceae")

fam_summary <- fam_summary %>%
  mutate(m_buffer_km = ifelse(family %in% m_families,
                              case_when(
                                family == "Orchidaceae"  ~ 10,
                                family %in% c("Bromeliaceae","Dryopteridaceae","Polypodiaceae") ~ 50,
                                TRUE ~ 25
                              ),
                              25),   # default
         m_buffer_source = ifelse(family %in% m_families,
                                  "SSC Colombia 2022", "Default (25 km)"))

fam_summary %>%
  filter(n_modellable >= 5) %>%
  kable(col.names = c("Family", "N modellable", "N B1 subset",
                      "M buffer (km)", "Buffer source")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

```{r endemic-pool-families-all, eval=pool_available}
#| tbl-cap: "All families in the endemic pool and their M buffer assignment"

  summarise(
    n_families         = n(),
    n_with_custom_buf  = sum(m_buffer_source == "SSC Colombia 2022"),
    n_with_default_buf = sum(m_buffer_source == "Default (25 km)"),
    pct_default        = round(100 * n_with_default_buf / n_families, 1)

                      "Default buffer (25 km)", "% using default")) %>%
